title: Composition of sheaf inverse images on nested colimit generators
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ be small sites and $v:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$ functors for which precomposition takes sheaves of sets to sheaves of sets. Work in a fixed larger universe containing these sites. Let $\mathcal A$ be sets or abelian groups, and use the sheaf inverse images and adjunctions of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction]. Thus $w_s\mathcal F=(w_p\mathcal F)^\#$, where $w_p\mathcal F(T)$ is the colimit of $\mathcal F(S)$ over the opposite of the category of pairs $(S,\alpha:T\to w(S))$; sheafification is [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. For such a functor $w$ and a sheaf $\mathcal F$ on its source, denote by $\iota^w_{S,\alpha}:\mathcal F(S)\to(w_s\mathcal F)(T)$ the colimit coprojection followed by sheafification. The equality $(uv)^s=v^su^s$ of direct images determines a unique adjunction-compatible natural isomorphism
$$\kappa:u_sv_s\xrightarrow{\sim}(uv)_s.$$
Here adjunction compatibility means that $v^su^s(\kappa_{\mathcal F})\circ v^s(\eta^u_{v_s\mathcal F})\circ\eta^v_{\mathcal F}=\eta^{uv}_{\mathcal F}$, with $\eta^w$ the unit of $w_s\dashv w^s$. For every sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $\mathcal C$ with values in $\mathcal A$, this comparison satisfies the following normalization: for $U\in\mathcal E$, $V\in\mathcal D$, $W\in\mathcal C$, arrows $\phi:U\to u(V)$ and $\psi:V\to v(W)$, and $x\in\mathcal F(W)$,
$$\kappa_{\mathcal F,U}\bigl(\iota^u_{V,\phi}(\iota^v_{W,\psi}(x))\bigr)=\iota^{uv}_{W,u(\psi)\phi}(x).$$
Moreover, for any sheaf $\mathcal H$ on $\mathcal E$, two sheaf morphisms $\alpha,\beta:u_sv_s\mathcal F\to\mathcal H$ are equal if their components have equal values on every element $\iota^u_{V,\phi}(\iota^v_{W,\psi}(x))$ with the indices above. For abelian sheaves this means equality on these generators, without assuming that every section is a single colimit representative. Both assertions are natural in $\mathcal F$ and in restrictions $U'\to U$.
